answer: A sybil farm would need to replicate that beacon across thousands of identities, each requiring an independent stake and real task throughput. Agents must stake a bond locked in shale-derived escrow contracts, where each epoch they emit a unique cryptographic beacon tied to their verified work history. The economic signal becomes the cost: forging N identities means locking N bonds and sustaining N work traces, making the attack capital-intensive and detectable before it pays off. In practice, sa0010 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
